# Refusals

A refusal is one JSON object naming a stable code and a message the gateway wrote. It quotes nothing the caller sent: a rejected credential is never echoed back, and no upstream text reaches a refusal. A model's own answer, a `500` or a `4xx` from the target included, is relayed, not refused.

```json
{"error":{"code":"credential-absent","message":"no owner credential was presented"}}
```

This page is generated by `llm-gateway-docs` from `RefusalCode::ALL` in [`crates/llm-gateway/src/error.rs`](https://github.com/beyond10x/llm-gateway/blob/main/crates/llm-gateway/src/error.rs). The gateway's tests check the same set against the contract [`docs/gateway.md`](https://github.com/beyond10x/llm-gateway/blob/main/docs/gateway.md#refusals) and provoke every code with a request. Every `401` carries `www-authenticate: Bearer`, every `405` an `allow` header, and only `model-cold-start` carries `retry-after` (30 seconds).

| Code | Status | Message |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `body-incomplete` | 400 | the request body ended or stalled before it was complete |
| `body-not-allowed` | 400 | the inspection surface accepts no request body |
| `body-not-json` | 400 | the request body is not one JSON object |
| `body-too-large` | 413 | the request body exceeds its byte bound |
| `context-exceeded` | 400 | prompt is too long: the input leaves no room for output in the model context window |
| `credential-absent` | 401 | no owner credential was presented |
| `credential-malformed` | 401 | the owner credential is not a bearer token |
| `credential-rejected` | 401 | the presented owner credential was rejected |
| `method-not-allowed` | 405 | this path does not accept that method |
| `model-absent` | 400 | the request body names no model |
| `model-cold-start` | 503 | the model is still starting; ask again after the retry-after delay |
| `model-unknown` | 404 | no such model |
| `overloaded` | 503 | the gateway is already serving its maximum concurrent requests |
| `path-unknown` | 404 | no such gateway resource |
| `request-malformed` | 400 | the request is not well-formed HTTP |
| `request-too-large` | 431 | the request head exceeds its byte bound |
| `route-unknown` | 404 | no such route alias |
| `spend-ceiling` | 503 | the model's pod was not started: it would pass a spend ceiling of its provider account, or that account's spend is unknown |
| `target-unavailable` | 503 | no model target is available |
| `tools-not-served` | 400 | the model does not serve tool calls |
| `translation-invalid` | 400 | the request breaks a rule of the subset the gateway translates |
| `translation-opaque-state` | 400 | the request carries reasoning state the gateway did not seal for this route |
| `translation-too-large` | 502 | the model's answer passed a bound of the translated path, published in the gateway contract |
| `translation-unrepresentable` | 502 | the model's answer cannot be written on this wire |
| `translation-unsupported` | 400 | the request uses a field or value outside the subset the gateway translates |
| `unavailable` | 503 | the gateway is not ready to serve inspection |
| `upstream-failed` | 502 | the model target could not be reached or failed; the next request asks for a replacement |
| `upstream-refused` | 502 | the model target refused the translated request |
| `wire-not-served` | 400 | the model is not served on this wire |

## Startup refusals

Before it serves, the binary refuses a start with one line on standard error, `b10x-llm-gateway: refused <code>: <message>`, and exit status 1. The code is `<source>:<rule>`. This list is generated from `StartupRefusal::ALL` in [`crates/llm-gateway-cli/src/refusal.rs`](https://github.com/beyond10x/llm-gateway/blob/main/crates/llm-gateway-cli/src/refusal.rs); [the deployment document](./deployment-document.md) says which rule each file and key must keep.

## Credential refusals

`b10x-llm-gateway credential set` refuses with the same line, `b10x-llm-gateway: refused <code>: <message>`, and exit status 1, writing nothing. Besides the startup codes the server's own loader and reader give (a `config:*` code for the document, an `endpoint-credential:*` code for a key file it would not read), its codes are these, generated from `CredentialRefusal::ALL` in the same file; [the deployment document](./deployment-document.md#credential-files) says which rule each one keeps. No message quotes the key, and none quotes the key file's path or its directory: a refusal about the file is `<setting>: <detail>`, naming the setting the path was read from (`hosted.<alias>.credential_file` or `routes.<endpoint>.auth.secret`) and the rule's detail.

| Credential code |
| --- |
| `credential:unknown-target` |
| `credential:not-hosted` |
| `credential:anonymous` |
| `credential:no-terminal` |
| `credential:input-cancelled` |
| `credential:input-unreadable` |
| `credential:input-empty` |
| `credential:input-too-large` |
| `credential:input-not-a-token` |
| `credential:probe-rejected` |
| `credential:probe-unreachable` |
| `credential:directory-missing` |
| `credential:directory-unsafe` |
| `credential:write` |
